learning_objective: 🎯 Master the naming words (Nouns) and their clever stand-ins (Pronouns), plus learn their special features like gender, number, and case!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A noun is the name of a person, place, thing, or idea. Concrete nouns are things you can touch or see, like a 'table' or 'dog'. Abstract nouns are feelings or ideas you cannot touch, like 'happiness', 'bravery', or 'freedom'.

main_concepts.concept_title: 🔢 Features of Nouns: Number and Gender
main_concepts.simple_explanation: Nouns have numbers (Singular means one, Plural means many). Nouns also have gender! Masculine (boy, king), Feminine (girl, queen), Common (doctor, teacher - can be male or female), and Neuter (book, chair - non-living things).

Imagine saying: 'Rahul grabbed Rahul's bag because Rahul was late.' That sounds silly! Pronouns like 'he', 'his', 'they', and 'it' take the place of nouns so we do not have to repeat the same names over and over. 'Rahul grabbed HIS bag because HE was late.'

Reflexive pronouns end in '-self' or '-selves' (myself, yourself) and reflect the action back to the subject (e.g., 'I hurt myself'). Relative pronouns like 'who', 'which', and 'that' connect a clause to a noun (e.g., 'The book THAT I read was amazing').

fun_activity.title: 🕵️‍♂️ The Noun vs. Pronoun Race
fun_activity.instructions: Take a short newspaper article. Highlight all the Nouns in yellow and all the Pronouns in blue. Then, draw a line from each blue pronoun to the yellow noun it is replacing!

quick_recap: ⭐ Nouns name people, places, things (Concrete) and ideas/feelings (Abstract).
⭐ Pronouns replace nouns to stop our sentences from sounding repetitive.
⭐ Reflexive pronouns reflect actions back to the doer, and relative pronouns connect clauses.
